Extractable cadmium levels in all samples from Tract III were less than 0.5 ppm. On Tract II, three samples were encountered with values greater than 1.0 ppm. It is unlikely that such levels are cause for concern.
Most intervals contained less than 2.0 ppm nickel, although values as high as 11.0 ppm were observed. It is unlikely that such levels would be phytotoxic.
The highest DTPA extractable lead concentration observed was 41 ppm, with most values less than 10 ppm. These values are within the ranges considered normal for surface soils.
Physical Characteristics - Samples from a number of holes were tested for water holding capacity. About one percent of the samples had water holding capacities less than 7.0 percent, the minimum value considered desirable in surface soils. It also appears unlikely that spoil materials may retain excessive water.
Soil texture influences aeration, rate of water infiltration, erosion potential and other important soil traits. Subsoils with greater than 80 percent sand are undesirable, and intervals containing greater than 80 percent sand were uncommon. Subsoils containing greater than 40-50 percent clay are undesirable. Overburden and interburden intervals containing excessive clay were found throughout both tracts, but in all cases the average clay percentage over the overburden plus interburden column was less than 40 percent.
